# Перенос функций FilmCraft в video-kadr

Дополнительный источник к продолжающемуся переносу WeftCut. Запрос пользователя: добавить функции из https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft. Оба направления остаются открыты; добавление второго источника не означает завершение первого.

Исходный snapshot: `5231852443363f001c3f6b396dd9b1e6461ae2be`, просмотрен 2026-10-08. Reference checkout: `/tmp/video-kadr-filmcraft-reference`. Изучены README, ROADMAP, структура crates, color/scopes contracts и алгоритм curve_lut в render/effects.rs; визуально просмотрены filmcraft-lumetri.png и filmcraft-scopes.png. Это история переноса и первоначальный групповой обзор. Конкретный runtime-каталог теперь в docs/filmcraft-catalog.json и docs/filmcraft-catalog-audit.md; полный аудит поведения каждого command/effect/codec ещё не завершён.

## Первый перенос: монотонные SDR RGB tone curves

`backend/src/domain/tone_curves.rs` адаптирует upstream Fritsch–Carlson LUT без выбросов, сортировку и dedup контрольных точек, flat plateaus и endpoint hold. Добавлена обязательная конечность/диапазон координат, максимум256points/channel, LUT2..4096, bounded GroupSurface и row cancellation. Master curve предшествует channel curves; alpha сохраняется. Native video preview принимает `tone_curves` в объявленном порядке effects и использует1024-entry LUT как upstream Lumetri. Display-encoded RGBA8 bridge — не полный linear-light/HDR Lumetri: transfer normalization/HDR grade space ещё не подключены.

Строгая wire model поддерживает master/red/green/blue. Export service/compiler явно отклоняет новый native effect до wiring native export, а не молча пропускает. Инспектор/анимация/import этого эффекта ещё не добавлены.

Лицензионное уведомление сохранено в `docs/licenses/filmcraft-MIT.txt`; MIT выбран из dual MIT/Apache-2.0 лицензирования. Кодеков/медиа/скриншотов в продукт не копировали. Нельзя переносить заявления README о полноте/скорости/bit-exactness на video-kadr; ROADMAP самого источника отделяет breadth от correctness и отмечает неиспытанные production media/platforms.

Проверки первого переноса: native curve2PASS (identity, monotonic/plateau, malformed/budget refusal, master→channel/alpha); actual authorized original-video preview API1PASS --nocapture (blue channel255→128); full backend571PASS3ignored + API63PASS; frontend typecheck0errors0warnings; git diff --checkPASS. Эти проверки не доказывают все перечисленные направления или HDR/GPU/браузерный curve inspector.

## Unified Lumetri contract identified during stage401

Pinned effects.rs lumetri (597–695) and lumetri_advanced (1080–1183) establish the source processing order: input LUT → linear white balance/exposure → signal whites/blacks → luma-weighted shadows/highlights → contrast/HDR specular → faded film → split tone → saturation/vibrance → vignette → look LUT (takes precedence over procedural look) / procedural look → tonal wheels → master/RGB curves → secondary HSL curves → HSL Secondary → linear premultiplied sharpen. Separate grading ranges apply to basic and advanced/HSL sections. FilmCraft retains a premultiplied linear f32 image across sections; host standalone effects currently quantize to RGBA8 between effects. Full unified parity therefore needs a shared float path and combined upstream oracle, beyond individual successful effect fixtures. Section switches and project LUT references are also distinct authored contracts. This source-derived requirement does not declare that integration implemented.

### Exact source scalar parameter authoring (2026-10-31)

The existing source-project panel now exposes a lazy scalar parameter editor for Float, Choice and Bool. It uses Rust `/api/compositions/filmcraft/parameters` and `/edit-parameter` routes against the opaque original document text. ### Executable source-video mask tracking (2026-10-31)

The source mask panel now runs forward/backward tracking with an explicit frame count, progress, Stop and a single accepted source-document history transaction. Each step calls Rust `/api/compositions/filmcraft/track-mask` against the opaque source document and authenticated library bindings. Rust resolves the clip/root-media identity, original source-frame clock, source bounds and tracking method; it decodes raw file frames through the existing revision-checked native video service, invokes the existing Shi–Tomasi / pyramidal Lucas–Kanade / deterministic RANSAC tracker, transforms positions and relative Bezier tangents, and writes exact signed-tick Path keys. JavaScript neither calculates motion nor increments source ticks. It passes the native returned cursor string to the next step.

All three source methods are executable: Position, PositionRotation and PositionScaleRotation. Source direction follows the original engine's source-time direction, including reverse clips. A frame hold has no available source-time tracking range. Seed and destination keys use original put-keyframe defaults; existing parameter/key siblings remain in the preserved document. A failed feature fit returns `lost` without inventing keys. Stop aborts the pending request and retains the successful prefix as one Undo operation; initial loss/boundary leaves the document unchanged. Unmount or document/session/source-binding changes discard the entire pending batch. The source panel passes its existing media bindings and token into this path. Library access is checked before decoding and before response publication; source revision checks prevent mixing frames from changed files. The original project filename is never opened as a server path.

Key times, interpolation and unedited siblings survive, and existing neighbouring handles stay unchanged (this is the original corner-insertion behavior, not a shape-preserving cubic subdivision). Empty animated key paths are refused defensively. Alt-click on a vertex toggles smooth/corner and Ctrl/Cmd-click deletes a vertex with the existing minimum-three-vertices guard.

### Match-source even dimensions and opaque H.264 output (2026-10-31)

Removed the even-source-canvas restriction from adaptive H.264 exports. The output dimensions now follow the original `max(2) & !1` normalization. Rendering uses output-width / sequence-width as its scale, then copies the resulting linear premultiplied image at (0,0), cropping or padding the right/bottom edges to the resolved canvas. This follows the original match-source Geometry branch rather than resizing the completed RGBA frame. Output geometry and render scale participate in the analysis cache key. The existing source/output size and memory limits still apply; invalid zero-size source canvases are rejected.

H.264 frames now use Filmcraft's opaque-over-black conversion: encode the already-premultiplied linear RGB directly to sRGB and write alpha 255. This corrects the previous straight-RGBA conversion, which could brighten translucent content when alpha was discarded by YUV encoding. PNG/FFV1 continue using straight RGBA. Placement remains inside the renderer's memory/cancellation accounting and releases the replaced buffer before the retained-storage invariant runs.

Reference: `crates/export/src/settings.rs`, `pipeline.rs` (Geometry/place), and `crates/render/src/image.rs` (over_black_rgba8), commit `5231852443363f001c3f6b396dd9b1e6461ae2be`. Fixed-size presets, fit/fill/stretch output scaling controls, remaining codecs, two-pass/HDR/surround and full original-app parity remain open.

Validation: the complete `filmcraft_image_sequence` integration target passed 26 tests (one ignored subprocess worker entrypoint is explicitly launched by the SIGKILL recovery test). New checks cover original dimension vectors, exact float crop/pad placement, exact quarter/half-alpha opaque sRGB bytes, renderer-storage release, and real MP4s for 241×180, 240×183, 241×183 and 1×1 source canvases. Each decoded raster is compared against an independently rendered width-ratio frame and independently evaluated linear-over-black sRGB conversion. The single-pixel padded border is exact black before encoding; after lossy H.264 its mean is checked near black rather than requiring every decoded pixel to remain zero. Existing PNG/FFV1, sequence clocks/tracking/cache invalidation, native audio, ownership, queue/retry/history, cancellation and killed-worker recovery cases all passed. ### Native PNG / TIFF / BMP sequences

Added the original three image-sequence presets to durable export, typed API and UI. The original still-writing algorithm is retained: PNG encodes RGBA8 (including alpha); TIFF and BMP convert straight RGBA to RGB8 by dropping alpha. Image canvases retain odd dimensions rather than applying video even-size normalization; custom geometry/quality/limiter still use the existing original rendering path with transparent output. Frame names start at zero relative to the export range, with `max(3, digits(count-1))` digits and original `.png` / `.tif` / `.bmp` extensions. Browser delivery is a ZIP of the actual numbered still files. Image-sequence requests reject audio, and selecting a sequence clears/disables stale audio selection in the panel.

Each frame is rendered then encoded in the bounded CPU pool; only the current encoded image is buffered. ZIP64-capable stored packaging streams to a UUID-owned staging file using shared deadline/cancellation-guarded I/O, syncs and publishes without overwrite. Native-export subfutures are boxed at the codec-dispatch boundary to keep the growing multi-format HTTP/job future within the runtime's ordinary stack. Completed results identify `image_sequence` and preserve ZIP downloads after later preset changes. No checked-in media fixtures or large numeric fixture tables were added.

Reference (MIT): Filmcraft `crates/export/src/lib.rs::encode_still` and `pcm.rs::image_sequence_path`, commit `5231852443363f001c3f6b396dd9b1e6461ae2be`: https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/tree/5231852443363f001c3f6b396dd9b1e6461ae2be/crates/export/src . Focused tests compare file bytes with independent calls to the original still-writing algorithm using the project's image dependency, and independently compare every decoded RGBA/RGB pixel at odd 7x5 dimensions. Real ZIPs with 1000/1001 frames qualify the numbering boundary; cancellation preserves peers/removes owned staging and an existing output is preserved byte for byte without invoking rendering. All three authenticated source-image jobs complete at a custom odd 57x43 canvas with FFmpeg capabilities disabled, reject audio, enforce owner-only downloads and finish staging cleanup. ### Native WAV 16/24 and AIFF 16 audio-only presets

Added the three original audio-only presets: stereo 48 kHz WAV 16-bit, WAV 24-bit and AIFF 16-bit. They reuse the existing source-project audio graph and original PCM quantization/header formulas, stream through the bounded CPU pool, and publish through the same durable queue, source snapshot, ownership, cancellation and no-overwrite path. Classic RIFF/FORM sizes are checked before mixing instead of wrapping 32-bit lengths. File encoding buffers 4096 stereo frames at a time; owned float-mix/staging files are removed on completion/error/cancellation. Cancelling a running PCM worker retains its CPU admission until the worker exits.

Audio-only ranges use source-floor sample boundaries: `[floor(start*48000), floor(end*48000))`, with the mixer starting exactly on that output sample grid. They require no video rendering and skip video geometry/canvas admission; an audio-only project with a 9000x6000 authored canvas can export. Optional legacy withAudio does not disable an audio preset. Results expose audio_only/audio mode, actual PCM duration/rate/channels/bit depth, and null video fields. The UI hides unused video/metadata controls, ignores their stale validation state, and retains the completed WAV/AIFF format when the current preset changes.

Source comparison found a shared output-rate discrepancy: upstream AudioOut::new clones the root sequence at the resolved 48 kHz output rate before evaluating DSP. The previous bridge evaluated DSP at the authored rate and interpolated afterward. Preparation now overrides only the runtime copy's root sample rate, preserving the authored document and nested sequence settings. The audiovisual WAV/FLAC/video regression reference was corrected to evaluate the original graph at the resolved rate without weakening its comparisons. Native export entry futures and the separate audio-only branch are boxed to keep the multi-format async chain within the normal runtime stack.

### Fractional-rate audiovisual PCM range fidelity

The video bridge now prepares audio on the same source-floor sample grid as AudioOut: begin at `floor(start*48000)` and emit exactly `floor(end*48000)-floor(start*48000)` samples. It no longer interpolates an initial fractional root sample or unconditionally rounds the duration upward. At 30000/1001 fps, one-frame ranges starting at frames 0/1/2 therefore carry 1601/1602/1601 source samples. The raster bridge accepts only the legitimate floor/ceil endpoint counts and still requires an exact float-file byte count; unrelated short/long PCM streams are refused before rendering.

Native MOV/MXF writers receive the full declared source PCM stream. Per-video-frame ceil counts are packetisation boundaries, bounded by the actual audio total, and finalization checks all declared input samples were consumed. The earlier MXF-specific pre-trimming was removed: the pinned original MXF writer owns OP1a frame wrapping and OP-Atom clip wrapping. This matters for OP-Atom, which retains every source sample and rounds its audio edit-unit duration upward when a fractional endpoint exceeds a video edit unit. Original OP1a instead writes its floor-based per-content-package sample pattern; a single excess source endpoint sample is not a second picture content package. Existing direct mux tests now supply actual original floor-range audio rather than an artificially ceil-padded input.

The focused regression passed 21 authenticated jobs: starts 0/1/2 with FFV1/float PCM MKV, ProRes HQ MOV, DNxHR HQ MOV, APV MOV, MXF DNxHR, MXF H.264 and OP-Atom. Every extracted float/PCM24 sample is compared to the original graph evaluated at resolved 48 kHz from a 44.1 kHz authored project. MOV retains the exact source count, OP1a matches the original fixed content-package sample count, and OP-Atom retains exact separate mono bytes plus original rounded clip duration. Owned staging is absent after each job and the authored project remains unchanged. Source references: pinned Filmcraft `export/audio_out.rs::AudioOut::new`, `export/job.rs::sample_at_frame`, `export/mxf_out.rs`, and `mxf/write/mod.rs` at commit `5231852443363f001c3f6b396dd9b1e6461ae2be`. Focused log: `backend/target/filmcraft-fractional-audio-native.log`. The full `filmcraft_image_sequence` integration target passed 57 tests, zero failures and one ignored recovery worker entrypoint (107.82s), including explicit pre-render refusal of 1600/1603-sample streams for the one-frame NTSC range. Logs: `backend/target/filmcraft-fractional-audio-{check,native,final}.log`. Native AAC/gapless fidelity, arbitrary export settings and complete original-app parity remain open.


### Export loudness normalization and compensated true-peak limiting

Added the original export loudness effect to audio-only and audiovisual jobs: optional integrated BS.1770-4 measurement, target LUFS gain, and the original look-ahead true-peak limiter. Defaults are disabled / -23 LUFS / -2 dBTP; effective limiter ceiling follows source clamping to [-24,0] dBTP, true-peak detection is enabled and release is 80 ms. The optional camelCase loudness request field is backwards-compatible with persisted work. Completed job results retain measuredLufs (null for unmeasurable input) and gainDb, and the UI displays this original pre-limiter normalization report. It does not claim a post-limiter output LUFS measurement.

The existing bounded source mix is cached as an owned float file. Measurement reads that exact mix in one-second chunks, then a second streaming pass applies the gain and native limiter. Only the true export range is fed as signal; zeros fill the look-ahead beyond the end, and initial limiter latency is discarded. This preserves duration and alignment without buffering or rerendering the full programme. Both passes use CPU admission and guarded I/O; cancellation retains admission until running work exits and removes only owned mix/normalization files. Disabled normalization retains the original PCM bytes and produces no report. Video-only, image and GIF exports omit irrelevant loudness controls; stale hidden values do not block them.

The native meter and dynamics source Git blobs match pinned Filmcraft commit `5231852443363f001c3f6b396dd9b1e6461ae2be`. Independently isolated original tests passed 15 loudness/calibration/gating tests plus 3 limiter bounds/transparency tests. The temporary isolated build directory was removed after completion. New integration tests passed source-equivalent single-pull versus streamed output byte comparisons for long/short signals and silence, latency compensation, true-peak bounds, finite-setting refusal, no-overwrite, cancellation during both measurement and processing, CPU-permit release, input/peer preservation and staging cleanup. Authenticated WAV24 and ProRes jobs compare every normalized PCM24 byte and measured report with the original algorithm, and compare disabled output with the original raw bus. The authored 44.1 kHz document is preserved while the graph runs at resolved 48 kHz. UI/source-panel/API tests passed 142 tests, typecheck had no errors/warnings and changed controls/tests ESLint passed.

and upstream tests are vendored under `backend/vendor/filmcraft-aac`; Cargo
inheritance is adapted locally and global rayon remains disabled. All 16 Rust
source/test Git blob hashes match the pinned original. No media corpus copied.

H.264 MP4 with audio now uses original Rust AAC-LC encoding and the native MP4
writer, including CBR video with audio. The bridge's current stereo 48 kHz /
320 kbps defaults remain; configurable audio rates, mono/surround and other
untransferred audio settings remain open. AAC/AVC encoding and muxing no longer
require FFmpeg tool admission. Existing input-video decoding is a separate
service and is not claimed to be FFmpeg-independent.

AAC is fed bounded planar blocks from the prepared interleaved f32 mix within
the native CPU worker. ASC comes directly from the original encoder; the AAC
track uses media_start=1024. Complete original access-unit bytes are retained,
while the final sample duration stops at input sample count plus priming rather
than retaining zero padding as presentation time. Audio-enabled MP4 uses a 48 kHz
movie timescale so edit durations preserve individual audio samples rather than
rounding to milliseconds. The original encoder flush handles partial blocks;
finalization checks the exact declared source range. Native video two-pass
analysis consumes no audio; the final pass encodes audio once. Cancellation in
both phases preserves original PCM and peer outputs and releases worker permits.

Upstream qualification passed all 30 tests (17 unit, 2 decoder oracle, 6 encoder
oracle, 4 robustness, 1 doctest). These include real FFmpeg interoperability,
mono/surround, channel layouts 3–8, 8–96 kHz, quality and robustness checks of the
original codec; they do not claim those options are already exposed in the app.
Focused bridge qualification passed two tests: whole-input original AAC vs
streamed MP4 packets for 800 / 1601 / 1602 / 14000 / 30720 source sample frames,
exact ASC, priming and edit/sample durations, ffprobe metadata, actual decoded
non-silent AAC, and cancellation in both video passes. Raw decoder output may
expose up to 1023 padded tail samples; the published track duration/edit is exact.
The prior no-FFmpeg MP4 job test now also accepts native CBR MP4 with AAC.
Frontend: 150 tests passed; zero typecheck errors/warnings; export-panel ESLint
passes. Full export regression passed: 78 tests, zero failures, one intentionally
ignored recovery worker (160.36s). Logs: `backend/target/filmcraft-native-aac-native.log`,
`backend/target/filmcraft-native-aac-upstream.log`, and

### H.264 QuickTime MOV, AAC bitrate and PCM16/24

Reference: pinned Filmcraft settings.rs Multiplexer / AudioCodec / audio_codec,
export/lib.rs aac_factory, and original PCM quantization at
`5231852443363f001c3f6b396dd9b1e6461ae2be` (MIT).

H.264 requests now accept `multiplexer: mp4|mov` and `h264Audio` codec
(auto/aac/pcm), bitrateKbps and bits. Source policy is retained: MP4 forces AAC,
H.264 Auto selects AAC in both containers, and explicit PCM is available in MOV.
PCM bits resolve to 16 below 24 and 24 otherwise; AAC bitrate clamps to 32–512
kbps and the original per-channel cap. The existing stereo 48 kHz bridge remains;
additional sample rates, mono/surround and applying configurable audio policy to
other MOV codecs remain open.

The shared native H264Movie writer selects the original MP4 or QuickTime brand,
length-prefixed AVC and original packet timing. AAC uses the requested original
encoder bitrate with exact logical edits; PCM uses original signed little-endian
16/24-bit quantization and sample counts. Other native codecs retain their
existing PCM24 defaults. The request, persisted work, temporary/final filenames,
accepted container, completed audioCodec and authenticated download use the
selected container rather than the preset's previous fixed MP4 extension.
Audio staging admission accounts for raw input plus encoded PCM/AAC storage.

The panel exposes the H.264 container, AAC/PCM selection, PCM precision and AAC
bitrate, displays the effective codec, and omits inactive settings for other
formats. Switching to MP4 clears an explicit PCM choice in the panel; the native
API independently enforces original MP4 AAC policy.

Focused qualification passed three native tests: original codec/bit-depth/bitrate
resolution rules; complete AAC access units at 32/128/512 kbps and PCM16/24 bytes
from an independent original encoder/quantizer across MP4/MOV; and authenticated

path is retained; serialized older plans without width default to two channels.

picks; unavailable selected indices fall back to source channel zero. A mono

crossfade every channel. The clip input can feed the transferred surround output
stage with channel order L/R/C/LFE/Ls/Rs preserved.

### Mixed-width track/submix/Mix graph and compensation

The existing `SourceStereoGraph` / runtime now owns native two- and six-channel
buses per strip and at the master (the legacy Rust type names remain). Input
mapping and mono folding run only on two-channel strips. Pre/post insert racks,
mute and fader run at each strip's native width; output panning/conversion runs
after post-fader sends at the latency-compensated content clock. Sends use the
target width. Every compensation delay allocates all target channels, including
C/LFE/Ls/Rs, and graph output width follows the Mix. Source topological routing,
solo closure, pre-fader muted sends, absolute automation clocks, seek rebuild and
provider-failure recovery are retained. Older compiled graph fields default to
stereo, with the legacy pan path retained when output metadata is absent.

Nine core tests passed (1.18s): mixed stereo/5.1 tracks, mixed-width submix and
send matrices, mute/solo, six-channel volume/mute automation, input-map semantics,
look-ahead PDC across all channels, contiguous blocks, seeks, provider failure
recovery, mono fold to centre, old serialized stereo graph defaults, and actual
six-channel clip-runtime input feeding the graph without reordering, and pre/post
master insert racks processing all six channels. Log:
`backend/target/filmcraft-surround-graph-core.log`.

The six routing regression tests also passed, including 864 original stereo
routing cases and 660 original insert/seek graph cases (94.36s). Log:
`backend/target/filmcraft-surround-graph.log`. Full export regression passed:
85 tests, zero failures, one intentionally ignored recovery worker (181.05s).
Log: `backend/target/filmcraft-surround-graph-export.log`.

### Next source-backed gap: user export preset library

Audited pinned `crates/engine/src/export_tools.rs` (preset library and
`presets_*` handlers) and
`crates/engine/src/export_tests.rs::user_presets_persist_with_favourites_import_and_export`.
The host currently exposes fixed preset IDs in `FilmcraftVideoExportPanel` and
`VideoRequest`; searching host backend/frontend found no user preset library.
The missing feature includes these source behaviors, not merely another select:

- Unicode alphanumeric, case-insensitive name identity; built-in names reserved
  on save; overwrite defaults true, with explicit refusal when false.
- Save settings derived from a named preset plus overrides, stripping output
  path/range; category and description retained; user deletion removes favorites.
- List searches name, category and description; supports category, format and
  favorite filters. Favorite without a boolean toggles.
- Persistence survives a new session. The host needs owner-scoped persistence
  because it serves multiple authenticated users.
- Versioned `filmcraft.export-presets` JSON import/export. Source accepts versions
  up to 1, rejects another format and blank names, renames imported built-in
  names with ` (imported)`, and replaces same-key user entries. Import does not
  apply the file favorites; export includes favorites among selected entries.
- A saved preset must feed actual durable video export and retain settings after
  source-library edits, not just appear in a library response.

Acceptance must include authenticated owner isolation, persistence/reopen, name
collisions and imported built-in handling, filtered lists/favorite toggles,
export-delete-import round trip, and an actual custom-sized/rated export probe.
This feature is absent and remains open; existing durable job processing alone
does not implement the source ordered export queue/Quick Export commands.

### 2026-11-02: source queue/Quick Export audit and catalog reconciliation

Pinned export_tools.rs shows Quick Export remembers its last explicit preset,
initially DEFAULT_PRESET, resolves active sequence and default In/Out range,
then starts an ordinary job. Default Out is inclusive (+one source-frame duration);
without Out the sequence duration is used, with a minimum of one source frame.
Output-grid frames use floor(start)..floor(end-1)+1 at the resolved output rate.
Host SourceSequence::duration and filmcraft_export_clock::span already provide
underlying exact primitives; no Quick Export endpoint/state exists yet.

Source queue requirements still missing in the host:

- Add snapshots project/settings before execution, expands sequences x ranges,
  and validates the entire add before inserting its items. Ready items have no
  encoding job until start; one item encodes at a time.
- Start refuses an empty/non-ready queue. Stop drains the active encode and does
  not start another. Cancel-one marks Ready directly or cancels the active job;
  cancel-all also stops advancement.
- Retry accepts Done/Failed/Cancelled, clears prior job/error and optionally starts;
  Ready/Encoding refuse retry. Remove refuses an encoding item.
- Move clamps absolute/relative destination across the full queue. Clear normally
  removes terminal items; clear-all refuses while an item encodes.
- Pump settles job results and advances ready items, reporting progress/status/ETA
  and completion/failure. Job snapshots, per-owner control and current source ACL
  must remain intact in the host adaptation.

### 2026-11-02 — source MCP command_batch over native Rust commands

`command_batch {steps:[{id,params?}],stop_on_error?:true}` is now advertised by
the claimed editor MCP bridge and runs the transferred command subset in Rust.
Native `command.batch` first deserializes the complete step envelope, then runs
commands in order. Results retain the source shape `{completed,failed,results}`
with `{ok,result|error}` per attempted step. The default stops at the first
command error; false continues. Prior successful mutations remain applied.
Empty batches succeed. This introduces no composition Undo or new batch command
in the sixteen-entry source command catalog; it is the automation wrapper for
that catalog. Nested batch helper IDs are not engine commands and refuse.

The editor forwards one transport deadline outside command params. Rust converts
it to a monotonic instant, rechecks it before each step and bounds each awaited
command. Expiry or server shutdown stops later steps even with stop_on_error=false.
An accepted owned export may continue after its wait times out; callers get an
unconfirmed-completion error and must inspect state before retrying. This does
not claim server cancellation of all accepted batch work on browser disconnect;
disconnect/context change invalidates client observation, and the propagated
deadline bounds subsequent native execution. Authentication is rechecked by the
existing leaf services for each step. Command params cannot extend that deadline.

The browser sends the entire batch in one call; it does not implement command
ordering or error policy. Partial results remain available while MCP `isError`
is true and the agent activity records an error. Existing atomic composition
`apply_batch` behavior remains a separate interface. Large source integer and
serialized-snapshot transport checks also apply recursively to batch arguments.

## 2026-11-02 — Tracking jobs through API/MCP

Registered `masks.track`, `jobs.list` and `jobs.cancel`; the native catalog now exposes 46 leaf commands. Tracking defaults to a real asynchronous owner/server-session job; wait:true waits for terminal state and returns exact documentText in status. Jobs.list combines owner tracking and actual Filmcraft export history. `{job:trackingId,snapshot:true}` retrieves a current/final tracking snapshot explicitly. Jobs.cancel checks ownership, is idempotent for finished jobs, and cancels tracking between frames while retaining all completed keys. Completed work is not implicitly evicted at quota limits; new admission is refused until explicit finished-only `{job,discard:true}` removes a tracking snapshot. Active discard refuses without cancelling or deleting it. IDs never reuse discarded values.

The host loads authorized library movies/stills/numbered image sequences or captured generators. Document file paths and client pixels are not used as media authority. Admission captures media identity and sequence catalog; decoding and snapshot publication recheck access and revisions. Snapshot retrieval also rechecks the whole sequence catalog, catching additions/removal/renaming after job completion. Changed sources cannot expose a stale tracked document. Movie analysis requests a 960-pixel maximum width independently of monitor thumbnails/full-preview limits; a real 4096x2160 movie decoded to 960x506 while full preview refused its dimensions. ## 2026-11-02 — Make/Edit Subclip and master conversion

Registered clip.makeSubclip and clip.editSubclip plus the native host query clip.subclipDefaults (98 native leaf commands, including this host dialog query). Source/project/timeline precedence and named-target enablement follow the original. The plan resolves the root media through the original sixteen-node bound, uses source marks/still preferences or the timeline clip's speed-derived source range, and retains the planned name/label. Explicit tick/frame overrides preserve precedence and null/wrong-type fallback. Names are not trimmed. Creation resets item metadata/split state, appends into the first root-parent bin found in original mixed child traversal order and replaces project selection with the new ID.

Editing retains item identity, name, metadata and top-level split points. Master conversion requires the direct parent to be Media, clones its complete media payload (including interpret/offline/proxy/identity), sets inclusive Out from the exclusive endpoint and copies only markers whose start lies in [a,b). A nested/broken/cyclic subclip can retain editable boundaries without conversion; conversion refuses when the direct media is absent. Allocation collision/exhaustion and i128 clock overflow are guarded refusals. These authoring commands never open source paths; live decoder/session cache invalidation remains a separate qualification boundary.

The dialog query adapts original subclip_defaults, adds exact ticks/rational clock and read-only edit-dialog data, and does not create document/history entries. Imports expose exact parent/bounds/restrict metadata. UI supports automatic/Source/project/timeline creation, original defaults, optional boundary/restriction overrides, tick/media-frame input and master conversion. Defaults can repair an invalid boundary draft. Accepted edits adopt exact source text with document/owner/source identity-clock/selection/local-context fences and one bounded Undo/Redo frame, including unchanged edits. Still preferences now share one owner across subclip dialogs, source seeks and placement.

Validated direct-parent provenance inherits an existing authorized library binding only for a converted file-media alias. It never treats the cloned file path as authority. Undo excludes inactive alias IDs from monitor/export/session payloads while retaining choices for Redo; project selection and source identity remain separate. Tests cover the actual export source map through conversion Undo/Redo.
